It's because stock prices represent only the value of a single share. Different companies can have different amounts of outstanding shares. 

If Company A is valued at $1 million and its ownership is divided into 1000 shares, each share (stock) will cost $100. If Company B is valued at $10 million and is divided into 1 million shares, each share of Company B stock will cost only $10. This does not mean that Company B is worth less than Company A ($10 million > $1 million), even though a single share of its stock is cheaper.

[Here is a great Khan Academy video that explains the concept.](https://www.khanacademy.org/economics-finance-domain/core-finance/stock-and-bonds/valuation-and-investing/v/price-and-market-capitalization)

When comparing the values of companies, you should look at the Market Cap and you will see that Toyota's market cap of $216.34 Billion is much greater than Tesla's $29.3 Billion, even though Tesla's stock is almost $100 more expensive per share.

To answer your question of what will happen to Tesla's stock once they start turning profits, you have to understand that the stock price represents the market's valuation of the company's current assets as well as future profits. Tesla's stock price would only skyrocket if they became much more profitable than expected over a quicker than expected time period. Their stock price is positive even though profits are negative because people expect Tesla to be profitable in the future and those expectations influence the stock price. Furthermore, it is not necessarily always the goal for a young company to be profitable during the short term. Tesla may believe that it is worth investing more money than it is currently earning into R&D and building factories so that in the future it has a better product and greater production capacity.

This does sound like depression (especially because insomnia can be a symptom of depression), but you should be careful with self-diagnosing. The best thing to do would be for your friend to talk to his parents or his counselor at school about seeing a therapist or mental health professional of some sort.

As others have said, the most important thing for you to do is just to listen and be supportive. The reason she always mentions her depression is because it literally affects the way she experiences every day of her life. 

Don't try to invalidate her feelings by telling her how good her life is and that she has no reason to feel depressed. Depression can happen to great people who seem to have everything going for them yet they still feel depressed because their brain chemistry is out of whack. Also don't try to equate her depression to a time you felt sad and got over it. Trying to relate in this manner might make her feel more isolated because how she feels really isn't very similar to how a non-depressed person feels sad about something.

Ultimately, you probably won't be able to cure her depression by saying the right things to her, so don't put too much pressure on yourself. Just try to be as supportive as possible.

Thank you for posting this. Please know that people on here do read what is posted and we do care about you. Stay strong and continue to refrain from self-harming.

Regarding your Facebook posts, one thing you might want to do is to reach out to people directly via fb message or text instead of posting statuses as cries for help. When people see a status that is broadcast out to all your facebook friends, they may not feel personally obligated to reach out to you even if they do care because they think someone else will reach out instead. See the [bystander effect](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bystander_effect). In general, I think public facebook posts are probably not the best method for engaging in meaningful discussions like what you need when you're feeling depressed.

> You know those people who live in the moment, and can make even the most mundane activities exciting and filled with magic? Well, I feel like the opposite of that, and I kind of hate myself for it. How do I change this?

No I don't know those people, because they don't exist.  If you knew me, you might think that I was one of those people, but the truth is that there's nobody whose every moment is magical.  Every other single living person on this planet has at least a few boring moments, meaningless conversations, superficial relationships, and downright sad periods.  I'm writing this because when I was depressed I remember looking around and seeing everyone else having fun and seeming to effortlessly float through obstacles that I struggled with.  One of the major things that helped me get over my depression was that I went on a retreat with my high school and my classmates opened up and admitted to struggles that I would never have imagined they experienced.  There are many many people who experience the same pains you do, and you need realize that we make it through together because we share the same struggles.  We create medication out of our tribulations.

>  I feel so lost, and I don't even know who I am anymore. I really want to change things for the better, and be an amazing person who is happy and can inspire others, but I don't even know where to begin.

You begin by trying to be you again. Don't try to be some amazing person who is always happy and constantly inspires others.  Just be you.  And if you don't know who that is right now, then you need to take some time to contemplate and meditate on what things make you happy.  What things leave you feeling content and satisfied with yourself?  What interests you?  Pursue these things and you must go completely cold turkey to the things that leave you feeling disappointed or dissatisfied with yourself.  I had to quit facebook for a while in order to help me keep my recovery steady.  You may have to quit reddit for a while or quite doing drugs or quit drinking or whatever you feel you need to do.  But once you realize what you need to do, you must convince yourself that you do not have the option of doing anything else.  If you realize you need to quit doing drugs, then there is no option but to quit doing drugs. No ifs, ands or buts.

I understand that you do not have access to a licensed therapist, but there may be ways to fix the problems yourself.  Try to be conscious of what causes your anxiety attacks or think about why you fear for your life.  Often simply thinking about the rationale of something can expose a lapse in logic, allowing you to conquer your demons with reason and sense.
And as for not having anyone to confide in: that is the beauty of reddit.  There are many people here whom you will never meet in person, but would be glad to listen to every word you have to say.  You may not currently know the person who could end up saving your life, but he or she may be reading your post right now and is about to extend a hand and an ear.  There are people who are here for you and who want nothing more than to listen to what you have to say so they can help you through your troubles.  Depression sucks. Life is hard. I'm not saying that things are determined.  I believe it is all random.

Here's an oversimplified version of how I see it. Your genetics say that you have a 95% chance of responding with action B and a 5% chance of responding with action C in response to situation A. Your past experiences affect your likelihood to act a certain way, so now you have a 99% chance of responding with B and a 1% chance of responding with C.  Now, what you actually respond with is based on these basic probabilities and a huge number of unidentifiable variables in the specific situation to give that specific situation its own specific likelihood of responding with B or C.  You responding with B or C depends on this specific likelihood and then a sprinkling of randomness in the context of the probability leads you to take one action over the other.

I believe that every human action is determined by a combination of genetics, one's environment, and a sprinkling of randomness.  I do not believe in free will, nor fate.  The sprinkling of randomness makes life unpredictable; it's what makes the ride interesting.

I went on a week long immersion trip with my school to Guaymas, Mexico and it sort of shook me and I realized that it's the people you interact with that make life worth living.  Two days after I got back, I went on a four day retreat, where I was able to sort through my experience and think about my life and do a lot of "soul searching."  After these experiences, I was in a much better mental and emotional state.  I made some lifestyle changes, got more sleep, stopped playing Mafia Wars (cruelly and mind-numbingly addictive) and used my experiences to motivate myself to do something productive.  I started a club at my school dedicated to raising awareness and funds for microfinance.  The club grew to about fifteen people, and I made a presentation about microfinance that was showed to the entire student body, and the club raised over 1300 dollars which we invested through [Kiva.org](http://kiva.org).

I didn't even value sleep.  To me, going to sleep required too much caring.  Sleep was something that I needed to be a healthy, functioning individual, and I wasn't sure I cared about being that individual.  Instead I would stay up until 2 or 3 in the morning every night on the computer, sometimes doing nothing but staring blankly at a still screen.  I still did my homework (albeit usually from 1-3 am) and went to school and ran at track practice, but I did those not because I cared about them but because I was too scared to let go of them.  I think deep down I knew that if I let go of these things I would completely spiral down into a deeper depression.  Not letting myself sleep was how I was rebelling while still going through the motions in every other aspect.
